lead_reference.caption_excerpt: #1 Sage Durvasa gifted a celestial Garland to Indra. Indra put the Garland on the elephant Irawatham and in-turn the elephant crushed it under its feet. The sage could not control his rage on the insult done and cursed Indra.

#2 Due to the curse, Indra became very old and weak, started to lose battles against Asuras. Devas became worried and went to Shiva and Brahma, and then collectively went to Bhagwan Vishnu and requested his intervention.
#3 Bhagwan directed devas to make peace with Asuras and churn the milk of ocean to get the divine nectar, which can keep Devas young and alive always.

#4 Devas made peace with the Asuras and with great pride carried the Mandara mountain for use as a churning rod. The mountain fell from their hands on the way. Bhagwan seated on Garuda, picked it up as if it were a tiny berry and installed it in the milk ocean
#5 With Vasuki, the mighty serpent as the churning rope, the Devas and Asuras started to churn the ocean. Bhagwan cleverly made asuras hold the head side of the snake and devas the tail side.

#6 While churning, due to self-weight, the mountain started to sink in the ocean. Helpless, Devas then prayed to Bhagwan, who incarnated as tortoise or Koorma and bore the weight of the entire mountain on its hard shell.
#7 Bhagwan lifted up the sinking mountain on Bhagwan’s back which was harder than a thunderbolt and more than a lakh of Yojanas in width.

#8 When the mountain was lifted up, the Devas and Asuras all churned with great force and enthusiasm. Bhagwan entering into both of them and also into the serpent Vasuki, removed their fatigue and energised them.
#9 Brahma, Shiva and other gods were wonder struck and sang in praise of Bhagwan, showering flowers from the heavens.

#10 Vasuki started to emit poison from its mouth and this made Asuras very uncomfortable and the heat was experienced by Devas a little also. as well to little. Bhagwan with compassion, the clouds were made to rain on the Devas but not on the Asuras.
